1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.Nf3 b6 5.Bg.strategy: Pins the knight on f6 against the queen, so it cannot leave for e4 without uncovering the queen to the bishop, and adds a second pin to the one on c3. Black has to untangle without giving White a free hand.

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.Nf3 b6 5.e3.strategy: Solid and flexible: it opens the f1-bishop's path to d3 and builds the centre. White accepts that the pinned knight cannot take on e4, so the black knight may settle there, and plans to challenge it.

Plants the knight on e4, where the pinned c3 knight cannot take it, and prepares ...Bb7 to support it. Black fights for the central square before White has built a centre, at the cost of moving the knight a second time.

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.Nf3 b6 5.Bg.strategy: Asks the g5 bishop at once what it wants: keep the pin by retreating, or trade itself for the knight. Black spends a pawn move but gets a clear answer before choosing a set-up, while the bishop on b4 keeps the c3 knight pinned.
